question: A project lead notices that Claude keeps giving the same wrong answer about the travel policy, always matching last year's rules. Both last year's and this year's policy documents sit in the project's knowledge. What best explains this?
options: A) Claude is drawing on the superseded document, so the fault sits in the knowledge, not the model.
B) Claude has invented the policy, since fabrication is the usual cause of a confident error.
C) Claude is biased towards older material and will always prefer whichever document is oldest.
D) Claude has contradicted itself within a single answer, which is the definition of an inconsistency.
correct_answers: A) Claude is drawing on the superseded document, so the fault sits in the knowledge, not the model.
explanations: Correct. A repeatable answer that matches an old document is being read from that document. No amount of reprompting fixes an out-of-date source that is still available to be used.
Incorrect. Fabrication produces varied invented detail, not the same answer every time that happens to match a real superseded document.
Incorrect. There is no such preference for age. The problem is that two conflicting versions are both present and nothing marks which is current.
Incorrect. Nothing here describes two conflicting statements inside one response; the answers are consistent and consistently wrong.
